title: SGP4 propagation
summary: From a parsed element set to a state vector: element preparation, branch selection, and the propagation itself.

nodes.label: TwoLineElement and GravityModel
nodes.summary: Mean elements as parsed from the element set, plus the gravity model they were fitted against.

nodes.label: Prepare mean elements
nodes.summary: Convert degrees to radians and revolutions per day to radians per minute, and recover the un-Kozai mean motion.

nodes.label: Elements propagatable?
nodes.summary: The eccentricity must be below one, the mean motion positive, and the recovered semi-major axis physical.

nodes.label: InvalidElements
nodes.summary: The elements do not describe a satellite the model can propagate.

nodes.label: Period at or above 225 minutes?
nodes.summary: Selects the deep space branch. The period follows from the mean motion.

nodes.label: SGP4 secular terms
nodes.summary: Apply the secular rates from the oblateness, and the drag decay of the semi-major axis and the eccentricity.

nodes.label: SDP4 deep space terms
nodes.summary: Add the resonance with the Earth's gravity field and the long period luni-solar perturbations.

nodes.label: Solve Kepler's equation
nodes.summary: Recover the eccentric anomaly from the mean anomaly by iteration, then the true anomaly and the radius.

nodes.label: Perifocal position
nodes.summary: Evaluate the position and velocity in the orbital plane.

nodes.label: Rotate to TEME
nodes.summary: Apply the argument of perigee, the inclination, and the right ascension of the ascending node.

nodes.label: Radius physical?
nodes.summary: A radius below the surface means the drag term has brought the satellite down.

nodes.label: State
nodes.summary: Position in kilometers and velocity in kilometers per second in the True Equator Mean Equinox frame.
